question: According to the Census of India-2011, which state has the largest gap between male and female literacy rates?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Census of India-2011, **Rajasthan** has the largest gap between male and female literacy rates.
 
• The literacy rate in Rajasthan for males is significantly higher compared to females, highlighting the gender disparity in education.
 
• Efforts have been made to bridge this gap through various educational programs and initiatives, but challenges still remain.
 
• The gender gap in literacy is an important indicator of social inequality and has implications for the overall development of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Census of India is conducted every ten years and provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters, including literacy rates.
 
• Literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged seven and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• Reducing the gender gap in literacy is crucial for achieving gender equality and empowering women in society.
 
• Various schemes such as the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan have been launched to promote female education in India.
 
• Despite improvements over the years, rural areas in Rajasthan still face significant challenges in terms of female literacy.
